input: I haven't been in the city long, so everything still feels a bit strange. Back where I come from I used to work with plants. Herbs, mostly.
draft:
Jessa Rook picks up a cloth and wipes down a spot on the counter that didn't particularly need it. "Herbs," she says, not looking up. The word sits between them without particular weight. She moves a cup a few inches to one side. "West District has its share of apothecaries and herbalists. People who deal in that sort of thing."

She lets the silence hold for a beat. "Not my trade, so I couldn't say who's good or who isn't. But there are shops."

A pair of merchants near the window push back their chairs and gather their coats. Jessa's eyes track them to the door — hands, coats, the settled bill on the table — before settling back. The common room stays warm and quiet. A draft whispers under the front door as the merchants leave.
